title: Out of the Depths of Woe
description: Out of the Depths of Woe in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 547, “The Bow in the Cloud”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Out of the depths of woe, To Thee, O Lord, I cry; Dark-ness sur-rounds Thee, but I know That Thou art ev-er nigh.

lines: Out of the depths of woe,
To Thee, O Lord, I cry;
Darkness surrounds Thee, but I know
Though late and seen through tempests, rise,
Like them I watch and pray;
Catch the first gleam of welcome day
For lo, the swift returning dove
Brings home the sign of peace.
Thy bow is in the cloud!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
